referenceOrganization.name: Redwood Glen Speech and Language Center

costSharing.agency: California Department of Education Special Education Division

justification.otherJustification: Permission supports continuity of speech-language services after district relocation.

other.explanation: Receiving provider requires the current IEP to coordinate language services.

purpose.otherPurpose: Continuity of special education and related services.

referral.explanation: Persistent decoding, spelling, and written-expression difficulty despite targeted classroom interventions.

background.history: Marisol received reading intervention in grades six and seven and demonstrated stronger oral language than written language performance.
background.currentPlacement: Grade 8 general education classes with daily specialized academic instruction and speech-language support.
background.parentObservations: Family reports that Marisol enjoys science and art but needs extended time and structured support for reading-heavy assignments.

evaluationResult.procedureDescription: Comprehensive psychoeducational evaluation including academic achievement, classroom observation, record review, and student interview.
evaluationResult.explanation: Results identify significant weakness in basic reading skills and written expression.

ideaDisability.explanation: Specific learning disability affecting reading decoding, reading fluency, spelling, and written expression.

analysis.adverseEffects: Difficulty decoding unfamiliar multisyllabic words reduces access to grade-level text and slows completion of written assignments.
analysis.educationNeeds: Explicit structured literacy instruction, vocabulary support, and written-expression scaffolds are required.
analysis.accommodation: Extended time, text-to-speech for non-reading assessments, and access to graphic organizers support meaningful participation.
analysis.otherInformation: Marisol demonstrates age-appropriate oral reasoning, strong participation, and sustained interest in environmental science.

determinantFactors.insufficientReading: Not a primary determinant; documented systematic reading intervention was provided.
determinantFactors.insufficientEnglish: Not a primary determinant; English is the student's dominant instructional language.

primaryCauseExclusions.medicalExplanation: No medical factor accounts for the identified pattern of academic weakness.
primaryCauseExclusions.otherFactorsExplanation: Multiple measures support a disability determination independent of exclusionary factors.

specificLearningDisability.lackOfAdequateAchievementExplanation: Achievement in word reading, reading fluency, spelling, and written expression remains substantially below grade-level expectations.
specificLearningDisability.learningSettingObservations: During independent reading, Marisol used context clues effectively but required prompting to decode unfamiliar words and complete written responses.

SpecialDiagnosisJustifications.TeamOverride: Multidisciplinary team reached consensus using convergent academic, observational, and intervention data.

decisions.adverseEffectIdentified: Disability adversely affects progress in grade-level English language arts and content-area reading.

identity.qualification: School counselor and IEP team participant

participantReport.procedures: Reviewed language sample, curriculum-based measures, teacher records, and classroom observation.
participantReport.observations: Marisol communicated ideas clearly in discussion but benefited from sentence frames when composing extended responses.
participantReport.conclusions: Structured language supports and direct reading intervention are educationally necessary.

iepEligibility.determination: Marisol meets IDEA eligibility criteria for specific learning disability and requires specially designed instruction.

enrollmentGradeLevel.explanation: Marisol begins the effective IEP period in eighth grade.

concerns.reason: Reading disability limits independent access to grade-level print and written demonstration of knowledge.
concerns.parentConcernDescription: Parent wants Marisol to build confidence reading extended text and independently organize written work.
concerns.studentConcernDescription: Marisol wants to read faster, write longer essays, and participate in science projects without falling behind.
concerns.background: Marisol responds positively to clear routines, visual models, and feedback that recognizes incremental progress.

personal.strengthsDescription: Marisol is curious, collaborative, verbally articulate, and demonstrates strong conceptual understanding in science.
personal.motivation: She is motivated by environmental science, digital illustration, and helping younger cousins with art projects.

needsList.need: Direct, explicit instruction in multisyllabic decoding, reading fluency, spelling patterns, and structured paragraph development.

performance.generalEducationDescription: In general education, Marisol participates actively in discussion but requires accommodations to complete text-heavy assignments and written assessments.

testResultList.diagnosticStatement: Achievement data show a pattern of strength in oral language and reasoning with significant weakness in foundational reading and written expression.

personalGoal.description: Increase independence when reading grade-level informational text and planning written responses.
personalGoal.successCriteria: Use taught decoding and planning strategies with no more than one adult prompt in four of five opportunities.

intention.overview: Marisol intends to pursue education and work connected to environmental design or conservation.

desiredOutcome.title: Environmental design learning pathway
desiredOutcome.description: Explore high-school science, art, and technology courses that support environmental design interests.

deficit.explanation: Specific learning disability interferes with decoding, fluency, spelling, and written expression.
deficit.consequences: Slow, effortful reading reduces comprehension stamina and limits completion of written assignments.

accommodation.description: Provide extended time and access to text-to-speech for non-reading assessments.
accommodation.rationale: Reduces the impact of decoding difficulty while preserving assessment of content knowledge.

summary.description: Marisol requires specialized academic instruction to access grade-level literacy tasks and demonstrate knowledge in written form.

accommodation.explanation: Use digital organizers, text-to-speech, and extended time for literacy-intensive work.

disability.explanation: Reading and written-expression disability affects independent assignment initiation and completion.
disability.consequences: Marisol may avoid lengthy reading tasks unless steps and available supports are made explicit.

accommodation.description: Use visual task checklists and chunked directions for independent work.
accommodation.rationale: Supports planning, persistence, and self-monitoring during multi-step assignments.

summary.description: Functional performance improves when Marisol receives predictable routines, visual organization tools, and opportunities to demonstrate learning orally.

accommodation.explanation: Provide a planner check and assignment chunking at the start of independent work periods.

consequenceOfDisability.curriculum: General education curriculum with specialized literacy instruction, accommodations, and related speech-language services.

specialCategory.explanation: Special education services are required to address a specific learning disability in reading and written expression.

annualGoal.currentStatus: Marisol reads unfamiliar multisyllabic words accurately in approximately 62 percent of structured opportunities and writes organized paragraphs with adult prompting.

goalType.additionalInformation: Annual literacy goal aligned to grade-level informational reading and written-expression access.

facilitator.contribution: Provide direct structured literacy instruction, monitor data weekly, and share strategy practice activities with family.

criterion.description: Given grade-level instructional passages and a writing prompt, Marisol will apply decoding and planning strategies independently.

metric.otherEvaluation: Curriculum-based reading probes, writing samples, and teacher rubrics.

parentAcceptance.explanation: Parent supports the literacy objective and home practice plan.

independentActionsList.independentAction: Use a digital planner to record assignments, deadlines, and selected reading strategies before leaving each class.

course.name: Grade 8 English Language Arts
course.courseContentDescription: Reading literature and informational text, evidence-based writing, vocabulary, discussion, and research.

progressReport.description: Marisol is making satisfactory progress toward independently applying decoding and paragraph-planning strategies.

measurement.explanation: Weekly curriculum-based probes measure accurate decoding of multisyllabic words and rubric-scored paragraph organization.

progressReport.explanation: Progress trend is sufficient to reach the annual criterion with continued direct instruction.

parentAcceptance.explanation: Parent agrees to the annual literacy goal and associated services.

accommodation.description: Extended time and text-to-speech for classroom and district assessments that do not measure reading decoding.
accommodation.rationale: Allows Marisol to demonstrate content knowledge without undue influence from her decoding disability.

applicabilityList.applicability: Use for English language arts writing, science, social studies, mathematics word problems, and district benchmark assessments.

standardsReference.assessmentTitle: California Assessment of Student Performance and Progress
standardsReference.subject: Reading

accommodation.description: Provide designated supports and approved accommodations consistent with the IEP.
accommodation.rationale: Provides equitable access while retaining the intended assessment construct.

accommodation.explanation: Quiet small-group location reduces distraction and permits approved accessibility tools.

achievementStandard.name: Grade-level achievement standard with approved accommodations

placement.placementRationale: Marisol can access the general education curriculum for more than 80 percent of the school day with specialized instruction and accommodations.

schoolDay.specificModification: Provide a daily 10-minute planner and assignment-organization check during advisory.
schoolDay.rationale: Supports independent completion of multi-step assignments and self-advocacy.

schoolYear.specificModification: Review regression and recoupment data at the annual IEP meeting before determining extended school year eligibility.
schoolYear.rationale: Current data do not establish a need for extended school year services.

outsideSchool.explanation: No specialized transportation is required; Marisol uses regular district transportation safely.

insideSchool.explanation: No specialized transportation is required within the school campus.

rejectedDetailList.explanation: Parent accepted the complete proposed IEP.

rejectedPlanElements.explanation: Parent supports implementation of all services, accommodations, and annual goals.

change.explanation: Added text-to-speech access for science and social studies assignments after a team review of first-quarter work samples.
change.reasonForChange: Expanded accommodation improves access to content-area instruction without changing reading-decoding expectations in literacy assessment.

amendment.explanation: Accommodation clarification approved by the IEP team.

rejectedPlanElements.explanation: Parent agrees that the amendment reflects Marisol's current access needs.
